items.headline: Acclaimed Visual Novel Studio Announces AI-Generated Quake Clone
items.excerpt: Mages, the studio behind Steins;Gate, unveiled Juggernaut, a Quake-style shooter it admits was 'developed' almost entirely with AI. The reveal drew a near-unanimous negative reaction from English-speaking fans surprised at how far the generative pipeline went.

items.headline: Professor Layton Fans Are Concerned After 'AI Slop' Presentation
items.excerpt: Level-5's studio presentation for the Professor Layton remake set off fan accusations of AI-generated art. Scrutiny follows the CEO's earlier claim that 'around 80~90% of games are made by AI.'

items.headline: Twitch Plans To Shove More AI Down Creators' Throats With Stream Coach Tool
items.excerpt: Twitch is testing an AI-powered 'stream coach' that watches broadcasts and suggests how creators can improve their channel. The rollout lands alongside questions about opting out of AI content training.

items.headline: Genshin Impact dev HoYoverse wins $112,000 in court after AI company stole 63 of its characters' voices
items.excerpt: A court awarded HoYoverse $112,000 after an AI firm cloned 63 Genshin Impact character voices with 'nearly identical characteristics.' The ruling is an early marker for how game voice IP is protected against synthetic reproduction.

items.headline: 'Claude Strife': DLSS 5 has escaped into the wild, and things are immediately weird
items.excerpt: NVIDIA's DLSS 5 neural rendering is now in players' hands, and early results swing from convincing to hallucinatory. Used subtly it holds up; pushed hard it rewrites character detail in ways artists never authored.

items.headline: DLSS 5 isn't just bad; it might be straight-up infected or possessed by demons
items.excerpt: A hands-on with DLSS 5's generative frame reconstruction in GTA 5 catalogues grotesque artifacts and invented geometry. It is a pointed argument that neural rendering is still overwriting art direction rather than serving it.

items.headline: TikTok Parent Reportedly Building AI Model to Rival Google's Genie for Real-Time Spatial Video
items.excerpt: Bloomberg reports ByteDance is readying a world model for generating real-time spatial video, positioned against Google's Genie. The company hopes it becomes a 'flywheel' for immersive, generated interactive content.

items.headline: 'Gen-AI Controversy Aside' Is A Wild Thing To Write In A Video Game Preview
items.excerpt: A critique of games press normalizing generative AI by bracketing it off as an aside in previews. The piece argues the 'elephant is still in the room' when a game's assets were machine-made.

items.headline: Blizzard Workers Secure Historic Contract Covering AI Use & Layoff Protections
items.excerpt: Blizzard's 1,900-strong union ratified a contract that puts AI usage under negotiation with developers. It is the first major studio agreement giving creative staff a formal say in how generative tools enter their pipeline.

items.headline: How ABCD Trains Large Gaussian Splat Scenes With Constant VRAM
items.excerpt: Researcher Ka Heng Shiu details Alpha-Composited Block Coordinate Descent, which partitions huge radiance fields while keeping full-scene context during training. It lets artists train city-scale Gaussian splat environments without VRAM blowing up.
